drivingQuestion: Were stains instituted to be lenient or stringent?

segments.he: אָמַר רָבִינָא: לֹא לְהָקֵל עַל דִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אֶלָּא לְהַחְמִיר עַל דִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּכְתָמִים עַצְמָן דְּרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: «Ravina says» that there is no contradiction between these two statements: The very institution of the impurity of blood stains was enacted so as «not to be» more «lenient than Torah law,» but «rather to be stringent beyond Torah law. But» since the impurity of blood «stains themselves is by rabbinic law,» the Sages were lenient in specific cases.

moves.summary: the baraita's stringency is relative to Torah law; the leniency follows from stains being rabbinic
moves.about: the institution of stains is stringent beyond Torah law, but being rabbinic it is applied leniently
